_comment: Delta-ML preset: TRAJECTORY work -- forces for dynamics on the corrected surface.
CLI flags still win over anything set here.
Generates its own structures: al_mode 'learn' samples with dynamics on the currently
corrected surface and labels the structures that leave the trained region. On-the-fly is
on, so each run stops at the first such structure instead of finishing a fixed length on
a model already out of its depth.
Acceptance criteria for this case are the gradient RMSE and the NVE energy drift. Do NOT
judge a trajectory model by how far it moves an optimised minimum: a lower RMS force
error does not constrain where the gradient vanishes, and on a floppy system that metric
looks bad however good the forces are.
lambda 1e-6 gave both the best drift (1.11 kcal/mol/ps against 1.56 for bare GFN-FF) and
nearly the best gradient error; 1e-8 buys a slightly better gradient at a drift equal to
al_temperature is deliberately above the temperature of interest: sampling happens on the
surface being learned, so the first cycle only ever visits what the base method considers
relevant. Heat mitigates that bias, it does not remove it.
